Had the text been admitted as a revelation by the founder, the case would have, of course, been different ; but as the composition of an uninspired writer, it could not so readily attain that distinction, particularly when there were riany works extant with, much higher claims to reverence and faith. If any reliance is to be reposed on Buddhist tradition, the simple Sdtras must be accepted to be the oldest records, compiled at the first convocation immediately after the death of.the founder, and acknowledged to comprise the Very ipsissima verbu of the great teacher. Works on ethics and philosophy were, likewisc, compiled at that time, and they got wide currency. And looking at them the last convocation cannot be accepted as the probable time of the origin of the Lalita Vistara. The third convocation or that which was held under the presidency of Asoka, is not open to the objection above urged. It was held long before the time of the Chinese translation, and there was ample interval between the two cvents to give time for works compiled in India, to attain full credit as sacred scriptures, and to go out of India in that garb of sanctity. It was, besides, convened expressly for the purpose of condemning schismatic doctrines and books, and for settling which of the books then extant were 80 authentic as to be accepted assacred. Itis open, however, to one serious objection. It is difficult to conceive that it was then for the first time that a biography of the.saint was thought of.
